_about: Expected textbook answers for the SN1/SN2/E1/E2 engine (docs/mechanisms-plan.md, 'Seed test set' and the confirmed course worksheet answers). Each case: substrate SMILES (+ its name, checked by namer.js so a wrong SMILES fails loudly), steps [{reagent, solvent, heat, site}], expect for the last step: lamps (unlisted = none), products [{pathway, smiles, name, rank}], stereospecific, flags, notCovered, activation (first step). Seed 22 (menthyl/neomenthyl) is left out until checked against the course textbook; worksheet cases are only here once confirmed from Peter's answer key. Ch 8 additions (docs/ch8-10-app-gaps.md "Seed cases", ids A-…): expect.addition = {intermediate, regio, stereospecific} from data/additions.json; product stereo racemic | mixture | null; classify = Q6/Q7 regiochemistry per reagent; reagentMatching noGuess = drawn molecule that must get no estimated SN/E box.

cases.note: Seed 6; since P0-3 the E/Z order comes from the anti conformers' MMFF energies (E-forming conformer ~0.6 kcal/mol lower).
Plan table says 'E1 + SN1'; the confirmed course rule (weak Nu, polar protic, heat) makes SN1 major with E1 competing.

Worksheet 3c rule (confirmed): 2° allylic chloride + NaOCH3/THF → SN2 major, inversion, stereospecific Y; E2 competing. The worksheet's exact structure isn't recorded in the plan, so this uses (3R)-3-chlorobut-1-ene as a representative 2° allylic chloride.
Worksheet 3d (confirmed): weak Nu in polar protic solvent with heat → SN1 major, racemic, stereospecific N; E1 competing.

Ch 6 test 2a (confirmed from Peter's annotated key, 2026-11-08): 3° benzylic bromide + NaCN, DMSO, 65 °C → SN1 (very stable cation; SN2 blocked at 3°), racemic nitrile. E1 shown as minor (course rule course_3_ab_aprotic_sn1).
Worksheet 4a–c (confirmed): three ethers via no shift, methyl shift and ring expansion. The answer key doesn't rank them, so no rank is checked.
Spike S1 and worksheet 3e (confirmed from the answer key: SN2, stereospecific Y): ring cis/trans with no R/S centre. SN2 inversion turns cis into trans.
Spike S1: inversion where the R/S letter does not change (CH2OCH3 outranks CN but not Br).
Spike S4 on a longer chain: E major, Z minor, terminal alkene minor; no E/Z on pent-1-ene.
A drawn reagent not in the catalogue: box estimated by the three rules, nucleophile taken from the drawing.
Worksheet 3a (confirmed from the answer key): the Fischer projection is (S)-2-iodobutane (I right, H left, CH3 top). SN2 with NaCN/DMSO inverts it to the (R)-nitrile; stereospecific Y.

Worksheet 3b (confirmed from the answer key): 2° alcohol with OH on a wedge, read from the drawing as (S)-pentan-2-ol. SOCl2/pyridine gives the chloride with inversion (Cl on a hash); stereospecific Y.

Worksheet 5 (confirmed from the answer key): 6-bromospiro[4.5]decane in EtOH with heat gives two ethers: no shift (spiro ether) and ring expansion of the cyclopentane into a decalin (ether at the ring fusion). The photo doesn't show which is marked major, so no rank is checked. Shifting the cyclohexane bond would contract the ring: not covered. Spiro/fused names come from PubChem, so substrateName is left out.
Ch 7 worksheet 9l / 13a (confirmed): methyl shift inside a ring. Regression for the stale getBond() in buildProduct, which made this product an alkane.
Ch 7 worksheet 10a (confirmed): same in a six-membered ring.
Ch 7 worksheet 9i (confirmed): cis; tBu equatorial puts Br axial with axial H on both sides, so Zaitsev.
Ch 7 worksheet 9j (confirmed): trans; only C6 has an axial H anti to axial Br, so NOT Zaitsev.
Ch 7 worksheet 9k (confirmed): Br equatorial in the locked chair; in the flipped chair the axial group on C2 is CH3, so the C=C forms away from it.
Ch 7 worksheet 10d (confirmed): SOCl2 inverts, Cl axial; only the tBu side has an anti axial H.
Ch 7 worksheet 13c (confirmed): SOCl2 inverts, Cl axial and trans to CH3; C2 has no axial H, so the C=C forms toward C4.
Two ring stereocentres drawn without wedges: the chair would be a guess, so the trans-diaxial check must not run and the warning stays.
Ch 7 worksheet Q5 (key + 3D prototype): C4 has one H; anti to Cl it gives only the (E) trisubstituted alkene.
The (3S,4R) diastereomer of Q5 can only give the Z alkene (anti-periplanar H).
Ch 7 worksheet Q4b (key): (3R,4R) gives (3E)-3-methylhex-3-ene.
Ch 7 worksheet Q4b (key): (3R,4S) gives (3Z)-3-methylhex-3-ene.
No wedges: E2 is stereospecific but the configuration is unknown, so both E and Z are shown with a note.
Ch 7 worksheet Q4c (key B): the two exocyclic E1 alkenes are E/Z isomers and must have different names (they used to share one).
